thread:
incident-bot: Pager — PROD alert: streaming-pipeline.high_tail_latency (p99) breaching SLOs in us-west-2. Affected: SSE and websocket streams showing stalls and chunking delays. Error spike window: 2026-03-15T10:07:xxZ. Paging oncall.

sam (oncall): acked, on it. pulling graphs now. :eyes:

mara (SRE): I see p95 from ~120ms -> ~1s, p99 ~340ms -> ~5.2s in the last 6m. Streaming stall metric (streaming.stalled_count) jumped ~12x.

jon (eng-runtime): logs show a bunch of upstream proxy 504s and socket write timeouts from stream-proxy: 
```
2026-03-15T10:05:12Z stream-proxy[pid=22] WARN client_write_timeout conn_id=0xabc status=504 write_err=timeout
2026-03-15T10:05:13Z stream-proxy[pid=22] INFO chunk_flush delayed ms=876 conn_id=0xabc
```

jon (eng-runtime): also seeing clients with slow consumption (TCP recv window tiny) — looks like slow-consumer/backpressure. Some hosts show high socket buffer backlog.

mara (SRE): confirm which customers impacted? lee?

lee (support): quick list from alerts: acct-342 (chat widget realtime), acct-998 (live transcripts), a handful of PLG users on us-west. No billing or data loss reports yet, mostly stalls + reconnections. Customers are seeing long pauses in live responses.

sam (oncall): immediate mitigation proposals: 1) reduce stream-proxy chunk flush interval on a subset of hosts (fast flush), 2) bump keepalive/timeout to avoid proxy prematurely closing slow clients, 3) rate-limit slow consumers per-connection (drop after X total buffer growth), 4) route heavy streaming traffic to streaming-node-pool only (avoid overloaded general pool). Which can we do quickly?

jon (eng-runtime): we can do (1) and (4) quickly: deploy config change to streaming pool using canary env tag. Config snippet: 
```
# stream-proxy.conf (canary)
chunked_flush_interval_ms=50
max_client_buffer_bytes=8MB
upstream_pool=streaming-node-pool
```
Deploy to 2/8 hosts as canary and watch.

mara (SRE): ops-lead, recommend also restarting stream-proxy on the 3 most overloaded hosts after canary is green — that will free kernel buffers. Rolling restart only, staggered.

ops-lead: agree. I'll schedule rolling restarts with 60s spacing. tagging sam and jon.

sam (oncall): applying canary now. will post metrics in 90s.

incident-bot: action_taken: canary_config_deployed user=sam target=streaming-node-pool hosts=2/8

sam (oncall): canary looks good: p95 dropped ~40% for canary hosts, stalled_count for those hosts down to baseline. No error spike.

jon (eng-runtime): roll canary to additional 4 hosts. After roll, keepalive timeout increased from 20s -> 45s on proxy to reduce premature closes. Config applied via k8s configmap and reload.

mara (SRE): after roll: cluster p95 across streaming traffic dropped from ~1s -> ~210ms, p99 improved from ~5.2s -> ~650ms. Stalled_count overall down 70%. Good sign.

lee (support): notifying affected customers with status page note: "We're mitigating streaming stalls; responses may be delayed intermittently. Working on a fix. ETA 20-30m."

sam (oncall): doing rolling restart of 3 highest-load hosts now (stagger 60s).

ops-lead: restarted host stream-proxy-17, host metrics show buffer freed, inbound socket queue normalized.

jon (eng-runtime): added temporary rate-limit for slow-consumer connections: if client buffer > 6MB for >30s then send keepalive probe and if still slow, terminate connection with graceful 200+Reconnect header. Implemented as nginx upstream lua quick patch.

mara (SRE): re-checking SLO dashboard: p99 trending < 1s after rollouts and restarts. Will keep monitoring for 30m.

sam (oncall): tagging postmortem owners: mara (SRE) + jon (runtime). Please capture root cause hypothesis: slow consumer amplification + chunked flush tuning + proxy keepalive defaults too aggressive.

jon (eng-runtime): root cause notes to collect: kernel socket backlog metrics, netstat/TCP recv window patterns, client SDK versions (some older clients don't read chunked streams frequently), stream-proxy flush scheduling. Also correlate with recent frontend SDK release (v1.9.2) that changed read loop timing.

lee (support): will reach out to the top 5 affected customers with details and ask for client logs if possible.

mara (SRE): action items for postmortem: 
- revert aggressive keepalive bump after longer analysis (we'll revert to normal after a targeted client-whitelist)
- add automatic slow-consumer circuit break (server-side)
- add metric: per-connection buffer growth and emit early alert when >X across host pool
- evaluate backpressure-friendly changes in SDK (push small heartbeats from clients)

sam (oncall): status update to #oncall: mitigated, customer-impact limited, monitoring. Handoff to next oncall in 2h — if anything reappears escalate.

incident-bot: incident update: severity=sev2 impact=degraded_streaming duration=~18m mitigation=rolling-config+restart+rate-limit owners=mara,jon

lee (support): posting status page update and sending follow-ups to customers.

mara (SRE): leaving notes for postmortem doc: collect heap profiles for stream-proxy, tcp stats, client-user-agent distribution, and change log for SDK 1.9.2.

jon (eng-runtime): I'll open a PR with the canary config + automated canary rollout playbook and add healthchecks for chunked flush latency.

sam (oncall): thanks team. I'll monitor for 30m then handoff. If p99 climbs back above 2s I'll re-page. :white_check_mark:

lee (support): thanks. customers pinged.

incident-bot: thread closed (mitigated) — please file postmortem under incidents/postmortems and tag remediation:streaming-backpressure.

ops-lead: handoff completed. next oncall: @alex.
